resources.string: Save a checkpoint first (train from scratch once).
Continuing from your saved weights (2000 more epochs)…
Removes the JSON file from app storage. This cannot be undone.
No saved checkpoint yet. Train once to create one.
Trains a tiny network on synthetic XOR data. No pretrained weights, no network.
When off, this app does not use the network. When on, HTTPS downloads, the assistant chat, and installs from URLs you enter are allowed. Plain http:// is disabled.
Training XOR from random init (8000 epochs)…
HTTPS enabled: downloads, assistant chat, and APK installs. Native TF Lite still comes from the installed APK.

TensorFlow Lite: bundled assets/models/xor_mlp.tflite unless you downloaded a replacement (HTTPS). Kotlin training is separate. Native JNI libs ship with the APK; update them by installing a newer APK you trust.
TensorFlow Lite inference (downloaded .tflite if set, else bundled):
Use a full APK update to replace native runtime libraries (JNI). Use “Download .tflite” to replace only the inference model file on disk.
Using bundled .tflite again; removed downloaded copy.
Saved model (%1$d bytes). TFLite runs use this file until you reset.
Allow installs for this app, then try “Download APK” again.
Each message includes this subject so the assistant can tailor library and model advice.
Turn on “Allow HTTPS downloads” on the main screen, then return here.
No bearer token — request sent without Authorization header.

Tab ML Box talks only to the HTTPS address you enter under “Your server settings”. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

Set “HTTPS base URL” to the origin of your own assistant service (must start with https://). The app calls POST /v1/chat/completions with JSON on that host.

“Bearer token” is optional: leave it blank if your server does not check Authorization.

This app cannot use plain http://. If your service runs at home on a private address, you must expose it with HTTPS and a certificate the tablet trusts (for example a small gateway you control).

The assistant cannot edit Gradle files on the device. It can suggest dependency lines for you to paste in Android Studio. It can suggest installing a .tflite file only when you or your server provides a real https:// link in the agreed format.
Installed model (%1$d bytes). Run TensorFlow Lite on the main screen to test.
No suggested .tflite in the last reply.
Messages go only to your configured HTTPS server. The assistant cannot merge Gradle dependencies inside the app.
Set your HTTPS base URL under “Your server settings” (must start with https://).
